name: RW Aurigae
what_it_is: a young star (a T Tauri star, still surrounded by a disk of gas and dust) that is known for irregular dimming and brightening

notes: Saturated in 304 of 333 images (OVERFLOW flag or empty core): too bright for SPHEREx, so no spectrum of the star itself is shown.

light_curve.what_is_plotted: a relative brightness index from the outer glow of the star image (not a magnitude), because the star is too bright for the detectors' cores
notes: Noise floor: a constant comparison star (Gaia G = 10.95) in the same images varies by only 0.03 mag rms (W1) / 0.05 (W2); the target varies by 0.24 / 0.40 mag rms (full range 1.0 / 1.6 mag).
Cross-check: the index follows NEOWISE profile-fit photometry (correlation 0.93 in W1, 0.98 in W2 over 23 visits).
SPHEREx points (synthesized at 3.4/4.6 µm from per-epoch spectra) are not possible: the star is saturated in SPHEREx.

what_to_look_for_in_the_movie: the star stays in place but its infrared glow changes from year to year
